title: Domain of a Radical Function: sqrt(1 - 2x)
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the largest set of real numbers on which the function h(x) = sqrt(1 - 2x) is defined, and express the answer in interval notation.

steps.title: Impose the Radicand Constraint
steps.explanation: A real square root exists only when the quantity underneath it is nonnegative, so the domain is controlled entirely by this single inequality.
steps.why: sqrt(t) is a real number exactly when t >= 0; for t < 0 the expression leaves the real number system.

steps.title: Solve the Linear Inequality
steps.explanation: Subtracting 1 and dividing by -2 isolates x; because the division is by a negative number, the inequality sign reverses.
steps.why: Dividing an inequality by a negative constant flips its direction, a rule that follows from the order-reversing nature of negation.

steps.title: State the Domain and Check the Endpoint
steps.explanation: All x up to and including 1/2 are admissible; the endpoint is included since the radicand equals zero there, which is a legitimate input.
steps.why: Zero under the radical gives the perfectly valid output 0, so the bracket at 1/2 must be closed.
